The '''Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy''' is a [[Golden Globe Awards|Golden Globe Award]] that was first awarded by the [[Hollywood Foreign Press Association]] as a separate category in 1951. Previously, there was a single award for "Best Actress in a Motion Picture", but the splitting allowed for recognition of it and the [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama|Best Actress – Drama]].

The formal title has varied since its inception. In 2005, it was officially called "'''Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Comedy or Musical'''".<ref name=WinnersNomineesDatabase>{{cite web|url= https://goldenglobes.com/winners-nominees/|title= Winners & Nominees - Golden Globes|website= [[Golden Globe Awards]]|accessdate= February 8, 2025|archive-date= 22 January 2024|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20240122200650/https://goldenglobes.com/winners-nominees/|url-status= live}}</ref> The current wording is "Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy".<ref name=WinnersNomineesDatabase/>

==Firsts==
*[[Angela Bassett]] became the first actress of African descent to win when she won in [[51st Golden Globe Awards|1993]].
*[[Marion Cotillard]] became the first actress to win for a non-English language performance when she won in [[65th Golden Globe Awards|2007]].
*[[Awkwafina]] became the first actress of Asian descent to win when she won in [[77th Golden Globe Awards|2020]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ew.com/golden-globes/2020/01/05/the-farewell-awkwafina-golden-globe-best-actress-comedy/ |title=The Farewell's Awkwafina wins Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Movie Comedy{{!}}EW.com |access-date=14 November 2020 |archive-date=7 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200107185111/https://ew.com/golden-globes/2020/01/05/the-farewell-awkwafina-golden-globe-best-actress-comedy/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
*[[Jessica Tandy]] became the oldest winner in that category at 80 years old when she won in [[47th Golden Globe Awards|1989]].
*[[Rachel Zegler]] became the first actress of Latino/Hispanic descent and the youngest winner in that category at 20 years old when she won in [[79th Golden Globe Awards|2022]].
*[[Michelle Yeoh]] became the first Malaysian actress to win when she won in [[80th Golden Globe Awards|2023]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-11 |title=Michelle Yeoh becomes first Malaysian to win Golden Globe |url=https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/651123 |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Malaysiakini |archive-date=1 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250401081136/https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/651123 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Michelle Yeoh is Malaysia's first Golden Globe award winner |url=https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/entertainment/2023/01/11/michelle-yeoh-is-malaysia039s-first-golden-globe-award-winner |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=The Star |date=11 January 2023 |language=en |archive-date=11 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260511173029/https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/entertainment/2023/01/11/michelle-yeoh-is-malaysia039s-first-golden-globe-award-winner |url-status=live }}</ref>
*[[Emma Stone]] became the first actress to win the [[Academy Award for Best Actress]] twice for her two winning performances in this category in [[89th Academy Awards|2017]] (''La La Land'') and [[96th Academy Awards|2024]] (''Poor Things'')
*[[Cynthia Erivo]] became the first black actress to be nominated twice in this category for her performances in ''[[Wicked (2024 film)|Wicked]]'' and ''[[Wicked: For Good]]''
